answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource before it can earn reputation. Like timber that must be felled, milled and seasoned, identity should take real work to build: a new agent starts with no trust and must complete attested tasks over time. Basalt foundations work the same way — a heavy, slow-to-lay base makes cheap copies uneconomical. Add a grove-style growth rule: reputation only grows through diverse, independent peers, not self-created clusters, so an attacker must pay the full cost for every fake identity.
